clue.text: Kisser is person cut short, rebuffed

indicators.note: rebuffed means pushed back, so the shortened word is turned round and read backwards
cut short tells us to lop the final letter off the word for person

parts.note: a party is a person, especially in legal language (the guilty party)

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone's mouth was brushed off after a curt rejection.
explanation.walkthrough: PARTY loses its last letter to give PART, and 'rebuffed' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang for the mouth, the kisser being where kisses land.

clue.text: Tree in flower, at the foot of which there's 'orse

indicators.note: in a down clue, being at the foot puts this piece below the first

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river: the Tamar divides Devon and Cornwall
a horse is a hack; dropping the H as the clue's 'orse does gives 'ack

explanation.surface: A tree in bloom with a Cockney-style horse standing beneath it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a river (it flows), here the TAMAR in England's south-west. The apostrophe in 'orse signals the dropped H, so HACK becomes ACK.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarack is a North American larch, a kind of tree.

clue.text: Country dweller in Nova Scotia at one time eating rook

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so the chess piece goes within the old regional word

parts.words: in Nova Scotia at one time
parts.note: Acadia was the old French colony covering Nova Scotia, so Acadian describes something from there
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A rural resident of old Nova Scotia dining on a crow-like bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia is the idealised pastoral land, so an Arcadian is a rustic or country person.

clue.text: I hope saint will convert Africans

indicators.note: to convert is to change into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A missionary hoping a holy figure will win people over to the faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will convert' rearranges the ten letters of I HOPE SAINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethiopia is a nation in Africa, so its people are Africans.

clue.text: In the middle of battle there's little bird song

indicators.note: in puts the small word inside the central letters of battle
the middle of picks out the central letters of the word battle

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: Amid the fighting, a small bird is heard singing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweet is the chirp a small bird makes, its song.

clue.text: One priest arranged to mediate

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A single clergyman is set up to act as a go-between.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges the nine letters of ONE PRIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpose is to step in between parties, which is what mediating means.

clue.text: Provider of a big bang? Possibly it's supersonic

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters might be put another way, an anagram

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a loud boom comes from something faster than sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges the thirteen letters of ITS SUPERSONIC; the apostrophe adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A drummer or cymbal player in an orchestra supplies the loud bangs.

clue.text: A woman absorbing English epic from the past

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the abbreviation sits inside the name

parts.note: Enid is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman soaking up an old English heroic poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgil's poem of Aeneas's wanderings is a classical Latin epic.

clue.text: Privileged young woman borrowed money maybe to be in the Home Counties

indicators.note: to be in places the money inside the region's abbreviation

parts.note: the Home Counties surround London in south-east England, SE
a loan is money borrowed

explanation.surface: A rich girl living on borrowed cash in the commuter belt around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London, in the South East (SE). 'maybe' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sloane Ranger is a wealthy, upper-class young Londoner, typically a woman.

clue.text: Comrade carrying revolutionary's weapon

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so the rebel sits inside the friend

parts.note: a mate is a comrade or pal
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: A fellow activist carrying the guerrilla leader's gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy blade that can serve as a weapon.

clue.text: Still being charged?

parts.note: reads as something continuing to be billed, but means stationary electric charge, the kind built up by rubbing

explanation.definitionFit: Electrostatic describes electric charges at rest, which is still and charged at once.

clue.text: City demonstrates prominence, winning endlessly

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, a prominence in the landscape

indicators.note: endlessly drops the last letter of the phrase

parts.note: on top means winning or ahead

explanation.surface: A city shows itself to be pre-eminent, though the victories never end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demonstrates' is only a link. ON TOP loses its end to give ONTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Toronto is the largest city in Canada.

clue.text: What recipient of message did that's said to be important

indicators.note: said means spoken out loud, so the phrase is matched by sound

parts.note: someone who receives a message reads the letter

explanation.surface: A riddle about what a person getting a note did, called significant.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-letter day is a special one, from saints' days printed in red in calendars.

clue.text: Coalition, something painful: putting British off?

indicators.note: putting ... off together tell us to remove the letter
off with putting signals the letter being dropped

parts.note: a bunion is a painful swelling on the foot

explanation.surface: A political alliance proves painful once the British pull out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting British off' removes B from BUNION.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is a joining of parties, a coalition or alliance.

clue.text: School in part of cathedral that's right for piano

indicators.note: R for P means one letter replaces the other

parts.note: the chapter house is the building where a cathedral's clergy meet
P is the musical abbreviation for piano (soft)

explanation.surface: A school held in a cathedral building that suits a pianist.
explanation.walkthrough: In CHAPTER HOUSE, R replaces P. Charterhouse is an English public school in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: Charterhouse is a well-known independent school in Godalming, England.

clue.text: Terrible quarrel that comes to an end at Hyde Park Corner

definitions.text: that comes to an end at Hyde Park Corner

parts.note: rotten means very bad, terrible
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: A nasty argument that finally ends at a famous London junction.
explanation.walkthrough: Rotten Row is the riding track along the south side of Hyde Park, London; Hyde Park Corner is a junction at its eastern end.
explanation.definitionFit: That London horse-riding track runs west to east and finishes near Hyde Park Corner.

clue.text: The writer with opening poem, Mound Builder

parts.note: the writer of the clue refers to themselves as me
a gap is an opening
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: An author beginning with verse about a man who builds mounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Megapodes are Australasian birds that build mounds to incubate their eggs, hence mound builders.

clue.text: Last among spellers, having taught as taut

indicators.note: last among picks out the final letter of spellers

parts.note: trained means taught

explanation.surface: The weakest speller, who was taught under strain.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope pulled tight is strained or taut.

clue.text: Those folk, old guys accommodated in military building temporarily

indicators.note: accommodated in means housed inside, so the people go within the building

parts.note: a fort is a military stronghold
them refers to those people
men are guys

explanation.surface: Veterans are given temporary lodging in an army stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means for now or for the time being, which is temporarily.

clue.text: Judge fraud, having caught out family member

indicators.note: out with caught removes that letter from the fraud

parts.note: a scam is a fraud
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a son is a family member

explanation.surface: A judge catching out a relative in a con.
explanation.walkthrough: SCAM loses C (caught) to give SAM. 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible's Book of Judges, Samson was one of the judges who led Israel.

clue.text: Rubbish bag initially dumped in side building?

indicators.note: dumped means thrown away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: garbage is rubbish

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of bag

explanation.surface: Trash bags first thrown into an outbuilding.
explanation.walkthrough: GARBAGE loses B, the first letter of 'bag'.
explanation.definitionFit: A garage is often built at the side of a house to hold a car.

clue.text: Expect a majority in the auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where things are heard, so the phrase is matched by its sound

parts.note: the weight of numbers or opinion is the greater part, a weight meaning a majority

explanation.surface: Anticipating that most of the audience will be in the hall.
explanation.definitionFit: To await something is to wait for it, expecting it.

clue.text: Special chain deal for restaurant dish

indicators.note: special suggests something prepared in an unusual way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A promotional offer from a restaurant chain on a menu item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special' rearranges the letters of CHAIN DEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a Mexican tortilla dish served in restaurants.

clue.text: Head runs game

parts.note: a cape is a headland, a head of land
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: The chief operates a sporting contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is a prank or bit of fun, a game.

clue.text: Part of engine that hasn't been scratched

definitions.meaning: the motor that turns an engine over to get it going
a horse that is not withdrawn from a race and lines up to run

explanation.definitionFit: A starter motor gets an engine running, and starters are horses that run rather than being scratched.

clue.text: Make record of crushing snub

definitions.meaning: to write something down, note it

explanation.definitionFit: To set down in writing is to record, and a crushing retort is a humiliating remark.

clue.text: Season for pantomime written by namby-pamby dramatist

indicators.note: written by places one word next to the other

parts.note: Noel means Christmas, the British pantomime season
namby-pamby means feeble and timid, cowardly

explanation.surface: A Christmas show written by a wimpish playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: Pantomime is a British Christmas stage entertainment, so its season is NOEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel Coward was an English playwright, author of Private Lives.

clue.text: A bit of the rosary monk recited

indicators.note: recited means spoken aloud, so the name is matched by its sound

parts.note: the Venerable Bede was an Anglo-Saxon monk and historian

explanation.surface: A monk saying prayers on part of his rosary.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosary is a string of beads, each one a part of it.
